 • THERESA MAE DULMAN 
 A 3-year-old child from Talisay City, Negros Occidental, died of dengue fever complications Oct. 18.
 The Talisay City Primary Care Facility said that a review is ongoing to establish the relevant facts surrounding the patient’s care and referral process, as it emphasized its commitment to transparency and accountability.
 “We remind the public that dengue can progress rapidly, particularly in children. Parents and caregivers are urged to seek immediate attention for warning signs, such as persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, unusual drowsiness, or difficulty breathing,” it said.
 Talisay City Mayor Rowena Lizares, in a social media post, condoled with the bereaved family and assured the public of a thorough review of the case.
 “I offer my sincerest condolences to the bereaved family. Bilang inyo Mayor kag isa man ka nanay , the loss of a child is something no one should ever have to bear,” she said. “A full and impartial investigation is sure to happen, including coordinating with the receiving hospital para mahibaluan naton ang mga natabo that led to this incident.”
 She urged residents to take dengue symptoms seriously, particularly among children, and to seek immediate hospital care at the first sign of illness. 
 The city health has appealed to the public to refrain from spreading unverified information while the official investigation is underway. | TMD
